grammarFocus: 转述动词；引述与改写；限定词 some / most / all 的范围。
title: The Community Newsletter: Reporting Sources and Checking Claims
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章是模拟的教育材料，不是真实的新闻报道。问题包括单选题、填空题和判断题（True/False/Not Given）。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。所有解释用中文。
passage:
A. The Maple Street Community Newsletter is a small monthly publication run by volunteers. Last month, the editor, Priya, received a letter from a resident named Mr. Chen. He claimed that the local council planned to close the community garden to build a car park. Priya wanted to report the story, but she knew she needed evidence. She asked Mr. Chen where he had heard the information. He said a friend had told him, and that friend had heard it from someone at the market. Priya decided not to publish the claim yet. She said, “We need to check this with the council first.” She also asked Mr. Chen if he had any documents or photos. He said he did not. Priya noted that the claim had no written evidence and came from an unknown source.

B. Priya called the council office. A spokesperson, Ms. Lee, denied the rumour. She stated, “The council has no plans to close the garden. In fact, we are investing in new plants.” Priya asked for a written statement. Ms. Lee promised to send an email. The next day, the email arrived. It confirmed that the garden would remain open. Priya also spoke to three gardeners. Two of them said they had heard the rumour, but they did not know where it came from. The third gardener, Mr. Patel, insisted that he had seen a council worker measuring the garden. However, he admitted that he did not ask the worker what he was doing. Priya thanked him and wrote down his words carefully.

C. Priya then interviewed a council worker who wished to remain anonymous. The worker explained that the council was measuring the garden to plan a new flower bed, not a car park. He added, “Some people misunderstood our work.” Priya also checked the council’s website. She found a document that mentioned a “review of green spaces.” The document did not say anything about closing the garden. Priya concluded that the rumour was false. She wrote an article explaining how the rumour started and what the council really planned. She included quotes from Ms. Lee and the anonymous worker. She also mentioned that most gardeners she spoke to were relieved. The article was published in the newsletter. Mr. Chen later apologised for spreading the rumour. He said, “I should have checked before I told others.”

D. Priya’s experience taught her an important lesson about reporting. She now asks all her volunteers to follow three rules: first, always identify the source of a claim; second, check with an official or expert; third, look for written evidence. She believes that these rules help prevent the spread of false information. The newsletter now includes a regular section called “Fact Check,” where readers can submit claims for verification. Priya hopes this will encourage more responsible sharing of information in the community. She also plans to train new volunteers in fact-checking skills. The training will cover how to contact officials, how to find reliable documents, and how to interview people who may be afraid to speak publicly. Priya believes that even small community newspapers can play a big role in stopping false news. She says, “When people know the facts, they make better decisions.” The newsletter’s next issue will include a guide for readers on how to spot false information online. Priya hopes this guide will help everyone in the community become more careful about what they share. She also wants to invite a local librarian to write a short column about checking sources. The librarian, Mr. Gomez, has agreed to help. He will explain how to compare different websites and how to find the original source of a story. Priya thinks this will be a useful addition to the newsletter.

questions.prompt: What did Mr. Chen claim in his letter?
options: The council planned to close the community garden to build a car park.
The council planned to build a new flower bed in the garden.
The council planned to invest in new plants for the garden.
The council planned to close the newsletter.
answers: The council planned to close the community garden to build a car park.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确提到Mr. Chen声称当地议会计划关闭社区花园来建停车场。
questions.evidence: He claimed that the local council planned to close the community garden to build a car park.

questions.prompt: What did Ms. Lee say about the council's plans?
options: The council has no plans to close the garden and is investing in new plants.
The council plans to close the garden next month.
The council is measuring the garden for a car park.
The council is reviewing green spaces for closure.
answers: The council has no plans to close the garden and is investing in new plants.
questions.explanation: 第二段中Ms. Lee否认了谣言，并说议会没有关闭花园的计划，反而在投资新植物。
questions.evidence: She stated, “The council has no plans to close the garden. In fact, we are investing in new plants.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the council worker say some people did? (Use one word from the passage.)
questions.explanation: 第三段中，匿名议会工作人员说“Some people misunderstood our work.”，即一些人误解了他们的工作。
questions.evidence: He added, “Some people misunderstood our work.”

questions.prompt: What did Priya find on the council’s website?
options: A document that mentioned a “review of green spaces” but did not say anything about closing the garden.
A document that confirmed the garden would be closed.
A document that mentioned a new car park.
A document that mentioned Mr. Chen’s letter.
answers: A document that mentioned a “review of green spaces” but did not say anything about closing the garden.
questions.explanation: 第三段提到Priya在议会网站上找到一份文件，提到“review of green spaces”，但文件没有说关闭花园。
questions.evidence: She found a document that mentioned a “review of green spaces.” The document did not say anything about closing the garden.

questions.prompt: What did Priya do after concluding that the rumour was false?
options: She wrote an article explaining how the rumour started and what the council really planned.
She called Mr. Chen to complain.
She started a car park project.
answers: She wrote an article explaining how the rumour started and what the council really planned.
questions.explanation: 第三段说Priya得出结论谣言是假的，然后写了一篇文章解释谣言如何开始以及议会的真实计划。
questions.evidence: She wrote an article explaining how the rumour started and what the council really planned.

questions.prompt: What did Mr. Chen say after the article was published?
options: He said, “I should have checked before I told others.”
He said, “I will never read the newsletter again.”
He said, “The council is closing the garden.”
He said, “Priya is a bad reporter.”
answers: He said, “I should have checked before I told others.”
questions.explanation: 第三段最后提到Mr. Chen道歉，并说“I should have checked before I told others.”
questions.evidence: He said, “I should have checked before I told others.”

questions.prompt: What are the three rules Priya now asks her volunteers to follow?
options: Identify the source, check with an official or expert, and look for written evidence.
Write articles quickly, interview everyone, and publish daily.
Avoid official statements, trust rumours, and ignore evidence.
Call the council, measure the garden, and build a car park.
answers: Identify the source, check with an official or expert, and look for written evidence.
questions.explanation: 第四段列出了Priya要求志愿者遵循的三条规则：确定来源、向官方或专家核实、寻找书面证据。
questions.evidence: She now asks all her volunteers to follow three rules: first, always identify the source of a claim; second, check with an official or expert; third, look for written evidence.

questions.explanation: 第四段提到通讯现在包含一个名为“Fact Check”的固定栏目。

grammar.title: 转述动词与限定词的范围
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，转述动词（如 say, claim, deny, explain, admit）用来引出别人的话。注意不同动词的含义：claim 表示“声称”（可能不确定真假），deny 表示“否认”，admit 表示“承认”。另外，限定词 some, most, all 表示范围大小：some 表示“一些”（不是全部），most 表示“大多数”（超过一半但非全部），all 表示“全部”。使用时要根据事实选择准确的限定词。
grammar.example: He claimed that the local council planned to close the community garden. She stated, “The council has no plans to close the garden.” Some people misunderstood our work. Most gardeners she spoke to were relieved.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: The witness ______ that she had seen the man near the bank, but the police later found that she was not sure.
questions.explanation: 句子后半部分说“但警方后来发现她并不确定”，这暗示她的话可能不真实，因此用 claimed（声称）最合适。denied 表示“否认”，refused 表示“拒绝”，admitted 表示“承认”，都不符合语境。
questions.evidence: He claimed that the local council planned to close the community garden.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: The manager ______ that there had been a mistake in the report, and he promised to correct it immediately.
questions.explanation: 句子后半部分说“他承诺立即改正”，这表明经理承认了错误，因此用 admitted（承认）最合适。denied 表示“否认”，与“承诺改正”矛盾；claimed 表示“声称”，不一定是承认错误；explained 表示“解释”，不如 admitted 准确。
questions.evidence: However, he admitted that he did not ask the worker what he was doing.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: ______ of the students in the class passed the exam, but not all of them.
questions.explanation: 句子后半部分说“not all of them”，说明不是全部通过，但通过的比例较大，因此用 most（大多数）最合适。some 表示“一些”，程度较轻；all 与 not all 矛盾；none 表示“没有一个”，与“not all”不搭配。
questions.evidence: Most gardeners she spoke to were relieved.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: ______ of the information in the article was checked, but a few details were missing.
questions.explanation: 句子说“but a few details were missing”，说明不是全部信息都被检查了，但大部分被检查了，因此用 most。all 与“a few details were missing”矛盾；some 表示“一些”，程度不够；every 不能直接修饰 of the information。
questions.evidence: Most gardeners she spoke to were relieved.
